newsitem.title: USA: News conference on tobacco delayed one hour.
newsitem.headline: News conference on tobacco delayed one hour.

text.p: A planned news conference on a possible settlement between U.S. states and the tobacco industry has been delayed until 2:30 p.m. EDT (1830 GMT) because of a snag in the negotiations, Arizona Attorney General Grant Woods told reporters.

He said Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp. was balking at any deal that included provisions to protect so-called whistle-blowers, employees of cigarette companies who provide evidence against their employers.
The news conference had been planned for 1:30 p.m. EDT (1730 GMT).
But Woods told reporters the dispute over protection for whistle-blowers was serious enough to threaten the talks.
"We are not going to leave the wounded (cigarette company employees) who have helped us, behind. This is nothing we're going to give in on," Woods said.
U.S. states and cigarette companies have been meeting since April to try to settle huge legal claims against the industry and agree on major new anti-smoking efforts.
